summary: ANISAI (*Listen to the Earth. Explore the Universe.*) is an accessibility-focused Earth science app created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It transforms NASA Earth Data Center satellite visuals—covering temperature, rainfall, sea ice, wildfires, and sea levels—into interactive pixel telemetry matrices. Using computer vision and the Web Audio API, ANISAI converts each pixel’s color, brightness, and movement into live musical pitches and rhythms. Powered by the "Hey Anisai" voice assistant, waveform visualizers, captions, and Sound Legends, users of all abilities can explore planetary data on desktop and mobile inside a deep-space interface featuring eight voice-switchable planetary themes.
details:
• How It Works: ANISAI streams satellite visuals (temperature, rainfall, sea ice, wildfires, and sea levels) from NASA’s Earth Data Center, converts each landscape image into an interactive pixel matrix, and uses computer vision and the Web Audio API to synthesize every pixel’s color, brightness, and movement into live musical pitches and rhythms—guided hands-free by the "Hey Anisai" voice assistant.
  • Benefits: It enables blind and visually impaired explorers to independently interpret complex Earth data through sound, while providing deaf and hard-of-hearing users with real-time waveform visualizers, live captions, and Sound Legends on both desktop and mobile.
  • Intended Impact: ANISAI democratizes Earth science so everyone—regardless of sensory ability—can experience our changing planet, raising climate awareness and advancing inclusive STEM education.
  • Tools, Languages & Hardware: Developed with JavaScript, Python, HTML5, CSS3, FastAPI, OpenCV, NumPy, HTML5 Canvas, Web Audio API, Web Speech API, React, and Pytest, running on standard PCs and smartphones using built-in microphones, speakers, and touchscreens.
  • Creativity: Rather than attaching pre-recorded music to space imagery, ANISAI turns raw planetary pixels into a live instrument featuring touch-drag pixel probing, dual-sensory waveforms, and eight voice-switchable solar system planetary themes.
  • Factors Considered: Our team prioritized scientific accuracy (grounding AI answers and sound mappings in calibrated NASA legends), preventing sensory overload with an audio complexity filter, blocking voice-assistant audio feedback loops, and building thumb-friendly 44px+ mobile controls.
